records.reason: m125 at 0/1, 50 uL sample and 300 uL DCM establishes the lower-volume side of a matched contrast. The 100 uL pure-EA pair e7ed7ca4a53258b73ba2/dd4f07e349873053fd73 differed by 10.89 mL in completion. This tests whether that association extends to lower sample loading.

m125 at 0/1, 50 uL sample and 500 uL DCM completes the matched contrast. Its prediction is almost identical to the selected 300 uL row despite completion differences at all three measured 1/1 sample loadings. The pair can teach a ratio-by-loading-volume interaction.

m127 at 20/1 and 150 uL tests whether the exceptionally early onset at 50/1 in c82167c626a1495ef750 is localized to that condition. The matched-ratio 50 uL anchor 8143c4fff6f999b7ad0e measured 15.38/31.14 mL. This distinguishes loading-associated onset changes from propagation of the unusual 100 uL interval.

m73 at 0/1 and 100 uL fills the loading midpoint between the early 50 uL result 9955b65d41bf10d27b48 and delayed, inverted 150 uL result 2732471e4009311396ed. The current 11.18/13.78 mL prediction interpolates that conflict; measurement tests whether such interpolation is useful.

This is a deliberate repeat of m73's recorded 0/1, 150 uL tuple in 2732471e4009311396ed, which measured 18.01/17.00 mL. Repeating the inverted record tests reproducibility before its delayed onset is generalized to neighboring loadings. It complements the selected 100 uL midpoint.

m207 at 10/1 and 150 uL extends the same-loading 5/1 result a7906197994af5c86745, 14.12/36.41 mL, and contrasts with the 100 uL 10/1 anchor ff3b6b1069b7d66ad021. This tests loading transfer beyond the exceptional short 100 uL 5/1 record without imposing a monotonic mass correction.

m60 at 2/1 and 50 uL starts a matched-loading comparison with the selected 100 uL row. At 5/1, 985361f6699d97f9464f and 62d7ea74ab73fa6214b4 differed mainly in onset, 27.63 versus 19.65 mL. This tests whether that association appears before the steeper retention transition.

m60 at 2/1 and 100 uL completes the contrast. Predictions barely distinguish the two selected loadings, while the measured 5/1 pair has an approximately 8 mL onset difference and a much smaller completion difference. The labels can teach ratio-dependent loading sensitivity separately for V1 and V2.

m53 at 20/1 and 150 uL bridges its same-loading 10/1 anchor 87d4aa727f2254c554ac and the much later 50/1, 100 uL result cdc8c1db00222994a1aa. The latter exposed a 32.37 mL acquisition-time completion underestimate. This locates response curvature while retaining the loading distinction.

m183 at 50/1 and 100 uL extends the same-loading 10/1 result cdd3b7758b3405a7b53f, 11.06/22.67 mL. Its predicted 22.40/45.03 mL response and high CW distance make it a useful comparison with the newly late unsaturated aldehyde m53, testing transfer across flexible aldehyde environments.

m21 at 20/1 and 150 uL probes the gap between the early 10/1 and late 50/1 low-loading measurements 487606cee9b08ded91f3/b4351e5f05f6d477a6c0. Its high CW distance supports investigating this transition. Loading differs from those anchors, so this informs joint prediction rather than an isolated ratio effect.

m97 at 50/1 and 50 uL extends the matched-loading 10/1 anchor 422ee7951888bafd55f4. The model predicts 13.59/29.33 mL, substantially earlier than the naphthylacetate result c80022254967f6a925f3 under its recorded conditions. This tests weak-eluent transfer within arylacetate esters.

m83 at 50/1 and 150 uL extends the same-loading 20/1 measurement cd52e7c2ec49986121e2, 9.74/20.23 mL. Alongside m97 and measured m98, it tests whether aromatic environment and ester substitution justify the predicted modest weak-eluent growth across this common ester family.

m162 at 10/1 and 100 uL bridges the region below the newly measured 20/1 and 50/1 responses ed3a90d38ff02a38deba/7b8eaa0c9205349f60b1. Those labels rejected the earlier predicted plateau. This point locates the transition and provides a same-ratio comparison with selected ortho-fluorobenzonitrile.

m163 at 20/1 and 100 uL forms a matched-loading ratio pair with its selected 10/1 row. Its 18.42/32.15 mL prediction has high CW distance despite a very small V2 quantile spread. The label tests the curve between early low-ratio observations and the later 50/1 reference 741f33ecf2e66f9958fd.

m194 at 1/1 and 50 uL tests loading transfer of its persistent completion tail. At 150 uL, d7895c522a1a46a1175c, e8185e062559aff5c99e, and 2bb48a2862bf80c30a36 finish near 25–28 mL across 0/1–2/1. This determines whether the learned broad interval extends to lower loading.

m129 at 0/1 and 100 uL tests the predicted completion increase to 18.20 mL from the 1/1 measurement b0571346163b8f77528d, 5.87/10.46 mL. Persistent strong-eluent tails are observed for some other aldehydes, but are untested here. This extends the question to an aryl thioether environment.

m118 at 0/1 and 100 uL tests its currently predicted 6.08/19.25 mL interval. Its 10/1 record 319e89d7000731f64e7f separated early onset from late completion, while 5/1 loading results also differed by endpoint. A pure-EA label constrains the strong-eluent end of this nonuniform curve.

m32 at 50/1 and 50 uL supplies the para-methylacetophenone side of a near-matched loading and identical-solvent comparison with selected ortho isomer m44. The measured bromo-isomer pair 605436d35600502e8c2e/a6f8e492c9e561c79cbd motivates testing whether positional response differences transfer to methyl substitution.

m44 at 50/1 and 50 uL completes the methylacetophenone comparison. Its predicted 8.25/24.39 mL interval is much earlier than m32's prediction, while the same-loading 20/1 anchor 4d75c120ba1c4f0dae89 measured 11.88/17.52 mL. This tests both positional transfer and the predicted endpoint-specific curve shape.

m131 at 50/1 and 100 uL tests weak-eluent growth for a dimethyl-substituted benzophenone. Its lower-ratio anchors include 64cada072f5110a54c64 and 18f616a941bed3e03bb0, while substituted benzophenones 44fcf641ccfa3b10a97c/1f40af3483bd97a7dfca span very different measured responses under their recorded conditions.

m106 at 10/1 and 100 uL is the weaker-eluent point of a selected two-ratio experiment for an ether-containing, CF3-substituted aryl ketone. Its pure-EA anchor 265b6eb5a10a34c937b1 does not constrain this region. High CW distance supports testing transfer from simpler aryl and alkyl ketones.

m128 at 20/1 and 50 uL extends the selected same-loading 5/1 point and measured 1/1 anchor b655d7de0986cbd0d622. Its aryl thioether plus ketone tests a sparsely anchored carbonyl environment. The aldehyde analogue's 20/1 record f4331eb64b6774466836 supplies a reference with different loading.

m47 at 5/1 and 150 uL extends its same-loading pure-EA anchor 02c053f1544310b38b17. The sterically hindered aliphatic ketonitrile is predicted to finish at only 12.35 mL, whereas aryl ketonitrile eb383b92fe958c91d272 was much later at 5/1. This tests motif composition beyond acceptor counts.

m75 at 2/1 and 50 uL fills an unmeasured strong-eluent portion of the phenylmalonate curve. Its 5/1, 10/1, 20/1, and exceptional 50/1 labels include d0c994e30d2f33948394, 9603a9567c8b21458d1e, 3726956d81fe3954e5b7, and 28e9fea3e3293f2b8a0e. This constrains where its nonuniform response begins.

m105 at 20/1 and 150 uL extends the same-loading 10/1 anchor fa64656d7b055dec7f56. Possible internal hydrogen bonding is a prior for this ortho-hydroxy ester, not an established mechanism. Comparison with exposed-OH ester 12ab195583f05b9aa177 tests topology-specific donor/carbonyl transfer.

m213 at 50/1 and 100 uL explores the weak-eluent response of dibenzyl ether. The 10/1 and 20/1 high-loading anchors e8d25b0f93b5bcf88daf/fa7b8202df1e985c228c have similar completion despite changing ratio. This tests the predicted modest extension in a noncarbonyl acceptor family.

m116 at 50/1 and 100 uL tests a sparsely anchored aromatic ether extension with high CW distance. Its 10/1 high-loading result 815afa4c05f8c4e7ef9c is modest, while dimethoxybenzene a47a3987d45e7c542d38 finishes later at 50/1 under different recorded loading conditions. This probes structural transfer beyond ether counts.

m122 at 50/1 and 100 uL extends a bromodimethoxybenzene with limited measured anchors, including 38c7016974af225a3cde at 1/1. Positional isomer m108 has 50/1 measurements b10935e1e299a91c24c3/dbbaf7572643228cf3aa. This tests weak-eluent structural transfer with the density/loading difference retained.

m163 at 10/1 and 100 uL supplies the lower-ratio point of its selected response pair and a comparison with m162 at 10/1. The two compounds have different recorded loading solvents and masses, so the labels test joint structure-condition prediction rather than an isolated F-to-Br substitution effect.

m106 at 2/1 and 100 uL completes the selected ratio experiment between its pure-EA anchor 265b6eb5a10a34c937b1 and selected 10/1 condition. Two labels can distinguish a gradual response from a transition missed by transfer from simpler ketones, while holding all recorded loading variables fixed.

m128 at 5/1 and 50 uL completes a same-loading sequence with measured 1/1 b655d7de0986cbd0d622 and selected 20/1. The predicted small initial change followed by larger growth is untested. This sequence gives more interpretable learning about a thioether-substituted ketone than an isolated weak-eluent endpoint.

hypotheses.content: Solvent-ratio responses and interval shapes require motif-specific and endpoint-specific learning. Recent ester, aldehyde, and ketone labels show different locations and magnitudes of response growth; exceptional reversals also prevent a shared monotonic endpoint correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A common retention shift can improve one endpoint or family while worsening another. Ratio bridges, structural comparisons, and short local curves can teach where onset changes, where completion expands, and which relationships transfer.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do m53 and m21 transition, does the para/ortho methyl-ketone contrast resemble the measured bromo contrast, and do sparsely anchored m106, m128, and m47 follow their predicted curves?

hypotheses.content: Strong eluent often gives early onset, but completion can remain extended and structure-dependent. m194's approximately 25 mL pure-EA completion confirms persistence of its tail across 0/1–2/1 at high loading; this does not establish the same behavior for every aldehyde or loading.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest m194 acquisition-time error was almost entirely in V2. Further labels should test structural and loading transfer of completion behavior without moving onset by the same amount.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m194 retain its extended completion at lower loading, and do pure-EA m118 and m129 follow their predicted completion increases relative to stronger-retention conditions?

hypotheses.content: Loading associations depend on ratio, structure, and endpoint. m207's 5/1 middle-loading record is much shorter than both loading brackets, whereas m60 and m135 show clearer loading-associated onset differences with smaller completion changes. A universal alcohol loading correction remains inappropriate.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Nearly loading-invariant predictions can miss endpoint-specific differences, but sparse exceptional records can also create misleading mass trends. Matched contrasts at adjacent ratios can identify transferable associations without asserting causality.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m60's low-versus-middle loading onset difference persist at 2/1, and does high-loading m207 follow a coherent 5/1-to-10/1 response?

hypotheses.content: Exceptional narrow or inverted intervals need local checks before their shapes are propagated. m127's nearly coincident 100 uL, 50/1 interval did not extend to either loading bracket: both brackets finished near 23.7 mL, but their onsets differed substantially.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest m127 labels rejected the earlier prediction's propagation of a late, narrow response to adjacent loadings. A nearby ratio can determine whether the remaining onset variation is localized, while repeated-tuple variation elsewhere limits mechanistic interpretation.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 150 uL, does m127 at 20/1 resemble the moderate-onset low-loading anchor or retain the unusually early onset measured at 50/1?

hypotheses.content: For m125, increasing DCM loading volume from 300 to 500 uL is associated with approximately 18–19 mL later completion at 1/1 across all three measured sample loadings. A smaller but substantial difference also occurs at 0/1 and 100 uL sample. The measured 5/1 pairs have similar completion, supporting a ratio-dependent association rather than a universal volume shift.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The current predictor still barely distinguishes the selected loading-volume pair. Additional matched labels can teach this recorded interaction and distinguish it from sample-mass dependence. The physical mechanism and contribution of unrecorded variables remain unresolved.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the pure-EA completion difference persist at 50 uL sample, or is its magnitude strongly dependent on sample loading?

hypotheses.content: The previous interpretation that m73's delayed onset is confined to 1/1 is weakened. Its repeated low-loading 1/1 delay is flanked by early low-loading 0/1 and 2/1 labels, but the latest high-loading pure-EA record is also delayed and has inverted endpoints. Reproducibility and localization across loading remain unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The current pure-EA midpoint prediction may reflect interpolation between incompatible loading anchors. One deliberate repeat and one midpoint can distinguish reproducible condition structure from variation that the recorded features cannot explain.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the 150 uL pure-EA delay recur, and is the 100 uL pure-EA response early, delayed, or intermediate?

feedback_interpretation:
The latest m125 results strengthen the loading-volume association: the third 1/1 sample-loading pair differed by 19.16 mL in completion, and the pure-EA 100 uL comparison differed by 10.89 mL. The new 5/1 low-loading pair again had similar completion. I therefore retain a focused matched pure-EA contrast rather than extending a universal volume correction.

The m207 150 uL result returned to later completion, leaving the short 100 uL 5/1 record between two later loading brackets. That weakens a simple mass-dependent explanation. Meanwhile, m60 and m135 showed more coherent onset differences with relatively similar completion, motivating a matched m60 comparison at an adjacent ratio.

Both m127 loading brackets rejected propagation of the middle-loading narrow interval, with acquisition-time onset overestimates of 19.07 and 29.68 mL. Their similar completion but different onset now motivate a single ratio bridge. For m73, early low-loading pure-EA and 2/1 labels support local flanks around the repeated 1/1 delay, but the new high-loading pure-EA inversion weakens broader ratio-only localization. I allocate one explicit repeat because its reproducibility affects interpretation of neighboring predictions.

m194 retained completion near 25 mL under pure EA, so strong-eluent tail learning remains useful. The m53, m21, m98, and m162 outcomes exposed additional weak-eluent or transition failures, while m11, m80, and several other bridges were comparatively close to their acquisition-time predictions. Current predictions have already changed after retraining; historical errors identify useful failure regions, not current residuals.
batch_rationale:
The batch concentrates labels where they can distinguish response shapes or interactions, while extending coverage into sparsely anchored families. The m125 pair tests a coherent recorded loading-volume association. The m60 pair and m207 extension test endpoint-specific loading transfer. The m73 midpoint and deliberate repeat address a conflict that could contaminate nearby predictions, and the m127 bridge limits generalization from an exceptional interval. These investigations are bounded parts of the batch rather than a commitment to explaining every anomalous record.

Ratio experiments cover the recently problematic aldehyde and ester regions, ortho-halobenzonitriles, a para/ortho methyl-ketone comparison, and two short curves for m106 and m128. Additional weak-eluent labels test arylacetate esters, benzophenones, a hindered ketonitrile, a hydroxy ester, and neutral ethers. These choices examine relationships likely to transfer across supplied rows, including cases where similar heteroatom counts conceal different topology or accessibility. Recorded loading-solvent and mass differences are retained in comparisons and are not treated as controlled structural effects.

I favor new condition information over accidental duplicate tuples, with the m73 repeat explicitly justified by its inverted endpoints. CW distance and quantile spreads support some choices but are not treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty; small spreads do not exclude informative failures. V2 minus V1 remains the physical elution interval. The expected benefit is better joint structure-condition prediction and separate learning of onset and completion across the Row-distribution, not improved chromatographic performance of these experiments themselves.
